html:
La Isabela, on the north coast of Hispaniola, was founded by Christopher Columbus in January 1494 on his second voyage. It was the first European town in the Americas built to last.

About 1,500 men came with Columbus, along with horses, cattle, pigs and sugarcane, the first of the plants and animals of the Columbian exchange. They built a church, a storehouse and Columbus's house of stone.

The town failed within a few years. Settlers fell sick, food ran short, and they quarrelled with Columbus and fought the Taino. In 1496 his brother Bartolomeo moved the colony south to the mouth of the Ozama, where Santo Domingo grew. The ruins are now a national park.
sum: La Isabela, on the north coast of Hispaniola, was founded by Christopher Columbus in January 1494 on his second voyage. It was the first European town in the Americas built to last.
